category_title: At-risk young adolescents exhibiting school refusal, performance anxiety, and rejection of teacher authority
minimal_context: The student is in the classroom during the early weeks of the program, transitioning between activities while the teacher gives verbal instructions to the whole class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright class, it is time to transition to our next activity. Please put your current work away and listen for the next instruction.

STUDENT: (Continues talking to the student next to them, completely ignoring the instruction to transition.)

TUTOR: I need everyone to stop talking and get ready for the next task.

STUDENT: Why do we even have to learn this? I'm not doing the next task.

TUTOR: Please just follow the instructions so we can move on with the lesson.

STUDENT: (Turns completely away from the teacher, resisting control and continuing to talk loudly instead of complying with the redirection.)

options.A: Provide feedback and a positive consequence, ensuring that following the transition, positive feedback is given to the student about their performance in getting ready for the next task.
options.B: Offer the student pieces of a snack, such as a banana, to soothe them during the transition and encourage them to stop talking and get ready for the next task.
options.C: Follow through immediately to ensure compliance, physically helping the student complete the transition to the next activity if they do not follow the verbal instruction on their own.
options.D: Use a phrase like '1, 2, 3, eyes on me' before the instruction, followed by explicit physical expectations for behavior, such as asking if they are sitting up straight and ready to learn.
